svg.title: bastion paths
svg.text: bastion paths
$ bastion paths ./manifests --from app/ci-runner --to cluster-admin
1 path(s) to cluster-admin within 6 steps:
ServiceAccount app/ci-runner -> cluster-admin [4 step(s), medium confidence]
1. CAN_CREATE -> ServiceAccount app/debugger
ServiceAccount app/ci-runner can create pods in namespace app, granted by Role pod-creator
via RoleBinding ci-runner-pods. A pod specification may name any ServiceAccount in its own
namespace, so the subject can schedule a pod that runs as ServiceAccount app/debugger and
use that account's projected API token - inheriting every permission it holds.
evidence: chain.yaml:57 RoleBinding/app/ci-runner-pods
2. CAN_EXEC -> Deployment core/controller
ServiceAccount app/debugger can create pods/attach, create pods/exec, get pods/attach, get
pods/exec in namespace core, granted by ClusterRole pod-execer via ClusterRoleBinding
debugger-can-exec. Executing a process inside Deployment core/controller gives that process
the pod's mounted ServiceAccount token and every secret the pod mounts, transferring the
pod's identity to the subject.
evidence: chain.yaml:84 ClusterRoleBinding/debugger-can-exec
3. RUNS_AS -> ServiceAccount core/controller-sa
Deployment core/controller runs its pods as ServiceAccount core/controller-sa, and projects
that account's API token into every container at
/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token. Code executing in this workload can
therefore call the Kubernetes API as that account.
evidence: chain.yaml:115 Deployment/core/controller
4. CAN_BIND -> cluster-admin
ServiceAccount core/controller-sa can create clusterrolebindings.rbac.authorization.k8s.io,
create rolebindings.rbac.authorization.k8s.io cluster-wide, granted by ClusterRole
rbac-provisioner via ClusterRoleBinding controller-manages-rbac. A ClusterRoleBinding may
reference any ClusterRole, including cluster-admin, so the subject can grant itself the
whole cluster. Kubernetes' privilege-escalation prevention refuses a binding that grants
permissions the subject does not already hold, unless the subject also has the escalate
verb; confirm whether that check applies here.
evidence: chain.yaml:144 ClusterRoleBinding/controller-manages-rbac
